Budget participatif

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Censored regression

Not plain regression, not classification: censored regression
Survival analysis is the tool for it, even if the event isn’t death

Firms closing (business demography)
Leaving unemployment or benefits
A household responding during fieldwork




projects <- projects |>
  mutate(opening_time = Surv(months, opened))


#> [1] 109.23333+  26.00000  103.00000   13.23333+  36.00000   61.23333+
#> [7]  23.00000   37.23333+



+ marks a censored observation: at least this many months

Many models at once

projects_res <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(rec = projects_rec),
  models = list(
    null = null_spec,
    cox = cox_spec,
    ranger = ranger_spec,
    rfsrc = rfsrc_spec
  )
) |>
  workflow_map(
    "fit_resamples",
    resamples = projects_folds,
    metrics = projects_metrics,
    eval_time = 1:96,
    seed = 1
  )



we take care of the procedural code, again: 4 models × 10 folds
you focus on the modelling choices: preprocessing, models, metrics

easier to review, easy to rerun when next year’s data arrives

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
section: Metrics at chosen points in time
text:
Metrics at chosen points in time

projects_metrics <- metric_set(
  brier_survival, brier_survival_integrated, concordance_survival
)

projects_res <- projects_wflows |>
  workflow_map(
    "fit_resamples",
    resamples = projects_folds,
    metrics = projects_metrics,
    eval_time = 1:96,
    seed = 1
  )



every month for the first 8 years
not longer: only the earliest editions are followed up beyond that, so estimates get noisy
Brier score: how close the predicted probability is to what happened, at time t (lower is better)
concordance: do projects that open sooner get shorter predicted times?

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Write your own: Royston’s D

royston_d_vec <- function(truth, estimate, ...) {
  # parsnip's linear predictor increases with time: flip to a risk score
  n <- length(estimate)
  scores <- qnorm((rank(-estimate) - 3 / 8) / (n + 1 / 4))
  beta <- coef(survival::coxph(truth ~ scores))
  unname(beta * sqrt(8 / pi))
}

royston_d <- function(data, ...) UseMethod("royston_d")
royston_d <- new_linear_pred_survival_metric(royston_d, direction = "maximize")

royston_d.data.frame <- function(data, truth, estimate, ...) {
  linear_pred_survival_metric_summarizer(
    name = "royston_d", fn = royston_d_vec, data = data,
    truth = !!enquo(truth), estimate = !!enquo(estimate)
  )
}



simplified: the real thing also handles missing values and case weights
yardstick also ships it: royston_survival()

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
section: Use it like any other metric
text:
Use it like any other metric

workflow(projects_rec, cox_spec) |>
  fit_resamples(
    projects_folds,
    metrics = metric_set(royston_survival, royston_d)
  ) |>
  collect_metrics()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   .metric          .estimator  mean     n std_err .config        
#>   <chr>            <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1 royston_d        standard   1.52     10  0.0678 pre0_mod0_post0
#> 2 royston_survival standard   0.355    10  0.0205 pre0_mod0_post0



OPTIONAL slide
needs a linear predictor: Cox, Weibull, boosted tree, but not the forests or the null model
royston_survival() reports R²_D, the explained-variation version of D

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Easier access to censoring weights

cox_parsnip_fit <- cox_spec |>
  fit(opening_time ~ budget + theme + edition, data = projects_train)

pred <- predict(
  cox_parsnip_fit,
  testing(projects_split),
  type = "survival",
  eval_time = c(12, 24, 36),
  add_censoring_weights = TRUE
)
pred$.pred[[1]] |>
  select(.eval_time, .pred_survival, .weight_censored)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   .eval_time .pred_survival .weight_censored
#>        <dbl>          <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1         12          0.808             1   
#> 2         24          0.476             1.10
#> 3         36          0.243             1.25



dynamic metrics (Brier, ROC AUC) need inverse probability of censoring weights
augment() already added them, predict() didn’t
so predict() |> bind_cols() |> metric() worked for concordance but failed for dynamic metrics
separate from the linear predictor work, not needed for Royston’s D

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Operations vs projects

A project can have many operations (sites), from 1 up to more than 200
At the operation level, operations are grouped within projects

Split by project: group_initial_validation_split(group = project)

Concordance is lower there: about 0.63

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Abandoned projects

About 5% of operations are abandoned: they will never open
That’s a competing risk; here we dropped them

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Data caveats

Opening dates are given to the month
The vote is approximated as 1 October of the edition year
Source: Ville de Paris, Budget participatif : opérations des projets gagnants et réalisations, opendata.paris.fr, licence ODbL

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Everything is an event?

Use the observed time as if every project had opened→ underestimates the time until opening


plain regression on the observed time
the projects still waiting are treated as if they opened today

title: What’s new for time-to-event data in tidymodels
text:
Drop the ones still waiting?

Only use projects that have opened→ throws away data, and biased: the slow ones are the ones still waiting


not missing at random
here: almost 40% are not open yet!
especially recent editions would be left with only their fastest projects
